svg.aria-label: Diagram: Policy Troubleshooter and Policy Analyzer compared by the question each answers, which policy types each reads, which principal types each accepts, their freshness and cost models, and the gap between them for questions about a group
svg.title: Policy Troubleshooter and Policy Analyzer: two halves of one question, split along the wrong line
svg.text: Two good tools for one question, split along a line that does not match how IAM is used.
Neither is a beginner or advanced version of the other. Different inputs, different policy types, opposite directions.
Policy Troubleshooter
“Can THIS principal use THIS permission
on THIS resource, and why?”
Reads ALLOW + DENY + boundary policies
The full #36 evaluation, done for you.
Principals: users, service accounts, agents.
NOT groups. NOT domains.
Live — including group membership as of now.
Says UNKNOWN rather than guessing NOT_GRANTED.
Policy Analyzer
“Who has which access, where?”
Specify one or two fields, learn the rest.
Reads ALLOW POLICIES ONLY, in scope
and its descendants. No deny. No boundary.
Principals: users, service accounts,
GROUPS and DOMAINS.
Cloud Asset API — best-effort freshness.
20 queries per org per day free, then SCC.
The gap: “can the platform on-call group deploy to this project?”
Troubleshooter evaluates everything that decides the answer — and will not accept a group as the principal.
Analyzer accepts the group — and cannot see the deny rule or boundary that removes the access.
Neither answers it alone. Analyzer for the grant, then Troubleshooter on a NAMED MEMBER for the
subtraction — holding in mind that the second answer is about a person, not the group.
Opposite freshness problems — and only one is obvious
Analyzer: best-effort, usually minutes, occasionally stale. You learn fast not to verify a fresh change with it.
Troubleshooter: TOO current. Group membership is always taken at the time of troubleshooting, and the
context it returns does not include membership status.
Denied Tuesday, troubleshot Thursday, reports GRANTED. Transient failure, or someone joined a group?
The tool cannot tell you, and does not flag the ambiguity.
Three things the Troubleshooter cannot see
Cloud Storage ACLs — not accounted for.
VPC Service Controls — not diagnosed.
Pub/Sub resource policies — unsupported.
Check each separately before concluding.
CONDITIONAL is an upper bound
Condition false → role dropped from results.
Condition true → included, marked TRUE.
Cannot analyse it → INCLUDED, marked
CONDITIONAL. So results overstate access.
Everything in this block argued for binding groups rather than people (#31, #32, #34). Follow that advice and your
access model is made of groups — and the tool that performs the complete evaluation will not accept one.
“Analyzer shows the group has it” and “the group can do it” differ by a deny policy nobody queried.
